_note: Umpire's Call questions, used in order by the daily job (one per week). Based on the MCC Laws of Cricket; check against the current Laws before adding new ones. Local playing conditions can differ.

questions.question: The ball hits a fielder's helmet lying on the ground behind the wicketkeeper. What happens?
options: 5 penalty runs to the batting side
Batter can be caught off the rebound
questions.explanation: 5 penalty runs are awarded to the batting side, as well as any runs already completed.

questions.question: A batter is caught off a no ball. Out or not out?
questions.explanation: A batter can't be caught off a no ball. They can still be run out.

questions.question: The bowler runs out the non-striker, who left their crease before the ball was released. Is it legal?
questions.explanation: Since 2022 this is covered under the run out Law. The non-striker is out if they leave their ground before the bowler would normally have released the ball.

questions.question: A delivery bounces twice before reaching the batter's popping crease. What's the call?
questions.explanation: A ball that bounces more than once, or rolls along the ground, before reaching the popping crease is a no ball.

questions.question: Can a batter be stumped off a wide?
options: Only if they've played a shot
questions.explanation: Yes. A batter can be stumped off a wide, and the wide is still added to the score.

questions.question: After a wicket, how long does the incoming batter have to be ready to face the next ball under the Laws?
questions.explanation: Under the Laws, the incoming batter must be ready within 3 minutes or can be given out timed out. Some competitions set a shorter time.

questions.question: A fielder catches the ball cleanly but their foot is touching the boundary rope. What's the result?
questions.explanation: The fielder is grounded beyond the boundary, so it counts as a boundary six, not a catch.

questions.question: The ball hits the batter's pad and then rolls onto the stumps, dislodging a bail. How is the batter out?
questions.explanation: If the ball breaks the wicket after touching the batter or their equipment, the batter is out bowled.

questions.question: The ball pitches outside leg stump and would have hit the stumps. Can the batter be out LBW?
options: Only if no shot was played
questions.explanation: A batter can't be out LBW if the ball pitched outside the line of leg stump.

questions.question: The bowler's front heel lands on the popping crease line, with no part of the foot behind it. Fair delivery or no ball?
options: Fair, the line counts as in
Fair, if the back foot is fine
questions.explanation: Some part of the front foot must land behind the popping crease, which is the back edge of the line. On the line with nothing behind it is a no ball.

questions.question: The ball lodges in the batter's pad. What happens?
options: Fielders can still take a catch
questions.explanation: When the ball lodges in a batter's clothing or equipment, it becomes dead.
